question: Why were Bell System telephones built to survive decades of drops and daily use?
options: Makers simply built things better then
Bell owned the phones and paid repairs
answer: Because Bell owned them. For most of the 20th century Americans rented their phones from the Bell System, which made them through Western Electric and paid for every repair. A phone that lasted thirty years was profit; one that broke was cost. Once customers could buy their own, throwaway phones arrived.
move: To predict how long a thing lasts, ask who pays when it breaks.
ask: To guess how long something will last, who pays when it breaks?
trap: Crediting the era's craftsmanship when the repair bill decided it.
reference: Wu, The Master Switch: The Rise and Fall of Information Empires, Knopf, 2010
